subtopic_detail: Interpreting a mildly raised prostate specific antigen in an asymptomatic man
stem:
You are the general practitioner seeing a 62 year old man who has read about prostate testing and asks to have it done. He has no urinary symptoms, no bone pain and no weight loss.

He has no family history of prostate or breast cancer and takes no medication that affects the prostate. He tells you he cycled 60 km two days before the blood test. On digital rectal examination the prostate is smooth and symmetrical with no nodules and no induration. His prostate specific antigen result is 4.6 micrograms/L against an age specific upper limit of 3.5 micrograms/L for his decade.

data_table.Examination: Smooth symmetrical prostate with no nodule or induration, abdomen soft, no bony tenderness
data_table.Investigations: Prostate specific antigen 4.6 micrograms/L (age specific upper limit 3.5); creatinine and full blood count within normal limits; urinalysis clear

lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Repeat the prostate specific antigen within one to three months
options.rationale: A single raised result is confirmed on a repeat sample taken one to three months later before any referral, because transient elevation from cycling, ejaculation, instrumentation or prostatitis is common (Source: PCFA and Cancer Council Australia PSA Testing Guidelines).
source_refs: PCFA and Cancer Council Australia PSA Testing Guidelines

options.text: Refer directly to urology for transperineal prostate biopsy arrangement
options.rationale: Biopsy on the basis of a single unconfirmed result exposes him to bleeding, infection and the detection of indolent disease that would never have harmed him (Source: PCFA and Cancer Council Australia PSA Testing Guidelines).
source_refs: PCFA and Cancer Council Australia PSA Testing Guidelines

options.text: Arrange multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging of the prostate now
options.rationale: Imaging has an established role in triaging men before biopsy, but it comes after the raised result has been confirmed and a specialist assessment has been made (Source: PCFA and Cancer Council Australia PSA Testing Guidelines).
source_refs: PCFA and Cancer Council Australia PSA Testing Guidelines

options.text: Reassure him that this level is normal and repeat it in two years time
options.rationale: The result sits above the age specific threshold for a man in his sixties, so treating it as normal risks missing clinically significant disease (Source: PCFA and Cancer Council Australia PSA Testing Guidelines).
source_refs: PCFA and Cancer Council Australia PSA Testing Guidelines

options.text: Start a five alpha reductase inhibitor and repeat the level in six months
options.rationale: These agents halve the measured antigen level within six months and would mask rather than clarify the abnormality, and he has no lower urinary tract symptoms to treat (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).

explanation.summary: Australian guidance offers prostate specific antigen testing every two years to men aged 50 to 69 who request it after being informed of the benefits and harms, with earlier and more frequent testing for men at higher familial risk. The threshold is age specific rather than a single figure, and the guideline uses the ninety fifth percentile for the man's decade to decide who needs further assessment. Confirming an abnormal result on a repeat sample is a deliberate step that avoids a substantial proportion of unnecessary referrals, since the marker is prostate specific but not cancer specific and rises with benign hyperplasia, prostatitis, instrumentation, ejaculation and cycling. When the raised level is confirmed, the modern pathway uses multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging to decide whether and where to biopsy.
key_points: Testing is offered two yearly to informed men aged 50 to 69
Thresholds are age specific rather than a single fixed cut off
Confirm any raised result on a repeat sample at one to three months
Cycling, ejaculation, instrumentation and prostatitis all raise the level transiently
Magnetic resonance imaging now precedes biopsy in the specialist pathway
explanation.pearls: Five alpha reductase inhibitors halve the measured prostate specific antigen within six months, so any result in a man taking one must be doubled before comparison with the age specific threshold.

sources.label: PCFA and Cancer Council Australia PSA Testing Guidelines
